items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: And Art Farmer lived overseas for a while, Idris Muhammad, and even the old guys, Louis Armstrong, Coleman Hawkins, you know because you know things are just different.

ctx.x: You made me think of Joe Williams performed here and he introduced one song and he said, “Blues frees the spirit.”

Yeah, yeah. It does, it does. And it really comes out of the old spirituals when people were singing and hopes for and prayers for a better day, better conditions. I saw a heart wrenching interview, I mean sometimes stuff just pops up on YouTube and I say, “Oh I’ve just got to hear this,” something popped up the other day, somebody interviewed Nina Simone after she had left the States and went to France I think when she came back and they were interviewing her. And they asked her, you know, “Why did you leave?”…
I want to ask you about a video I saw, it was a sextet I think of you at the Buffalo History Museum. I believe you were playing a composition called “Joy.” Does that ring a bell?
